reachability.4: Allowed behavior under the user's explicit instruction that KernelPatch dependency must not be a hard delivery constraint. Standard source enumeration excludes KernelPatch files and records kernelpatch_commit separately; delivery compares module tree and sources only. Keep the recorded build dependency as provenance; do not require the delivery gitlink to match. The fixture candidate was manually constructed; no new controlled build was run.
reachability.5: Requires forged/self-consistent candidate or import input whose source commit has no module and whose nonempty sources excludes module files; normal module_dir/source enumeration blocks creation.
reachability.6: Requires an omitted source-list member and corresponding recomputed identity; standard source_files automatically includes kpm_utils.h. Import verification checks the provided list but does not independently enumerate completeness.

prior_ancestor_rule.exact_recorded_fixtures: Cases 1, 2, 4, 6 have nonancestor delivery commits and would be rejected by the old ancestor condition. Case 3 is rejected by binding mismatch in both versions. Case 5 can have source == delivery because both commit-tree calls use the same tree, message, key and second; then the old ancestor rule also accepts.
prior_ancestor_rule.equivalent_descendant_paths_not_executed: Giving case 4 or 6's signed delivery source_commit as a parent satisfies the old ancestor check while retaining changed KP or missing unlisted header, so these holes are not established as newly introduced by dropping ancestry. A malformed absent-module candidate with delivery equal to its source also bypasses the old condition. This comparison follows the inspected old branch, not an additional experiment.
prior_ancestor_rule.conclusion: Keep content identity instead of ancestry. Case 4 is permitted; do not add a KernelPatch dependency hard constraint. Cases 5 and 6 describe malformed/omitted imported records, not evidence that current controlled candidates are invalid. Any module existence or input-list completeness recommendation must stay within that import-verification scope; do not restore ancestry as a remedy.
